findings.body: Every attempt succeeds because validation never removes or marks the matched code as consumed. The new integration test's single successful login therefore gives false assurance for a credential that is required to be single-use.
findings.failure_mode: A one-time recovery credential behaves as a permanently reusable credential in the external-storage test path.
findings.impact: Every attempt succeeds because validation never removes or marks the matched code as consumed. The new integration test's single successful login therefore gives false assurance for a credential that is required to be single-use.
findings.root_cause: The added validator performs a stateless membership check against the original raw-code list.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist consumption atomically when validation succeeds and add an integration assertion that immediately reusing the submitted code is rejected.
findings.title: The test user-storage provider allows the same recovery code to be reused indefinitely
findings.trigger: The same externally stored recovery code is submitted in two or more login attempts.

raw_findings.body: The successful user-storage update does not remove the old local credential. UserCredentialManager tries the external validator and then the local credential provider, so an old local recovery code remains usable after regeneration.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Two recovery-code sets remain active simultaneously, allowing authentication with credentials that the user believes were replaced.
raw_findings.impact: The successful user-storage update does not remove the old local credential. UserCredentialManager tries the external validator and then the local credential provider, so an old local recovery code remains usable after regeneration.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new external-storage success branch treats creation as complete without invalidating an existing credential of the same type in the alternative backing store.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When the external update succeeds, remove all locally stored recovery-code credentials for the user before completing the required action; also add a migration test proving that codes from the previous local set are rejected.
raw_findings.title: Regenerating recovery codes in user storage leaves the previous local codes valid
raw_findings.trigger: A federated user already has recovery codes in Keycloak's local federated-credential store, as all such credentials were stored before this change, and then regenerates codes after their user-storage provider starts accepting the recovery-code type.

raw_findings.body: The existing removal block calls removeStoredCredentialById for a model that can now be external. For a federated user that method targets Keycloak's federated credential store rather than the external CredentialInputUpdater, leaving the exhausted external credential configured. A later login can consequently reach the input bean with no next code and fail instead of initiating setup.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Exhausted credentials remain in external storage and continue to be reported as configured.
raw_findings.impact: The existing removal block calls removeStoredCredentialById for a model that can now be external. raw_findings.root_cause: The patch broadens the selected credential from local-only to local-or-external without adapting the subsequent local-only deletion operation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve whether the selected credential came from user storage and, when it is external, remove it through disableCredentialType or another external-provider operation; use removeStoredCredentialById only for locally stored models.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 80 shows getCredential now returns credentials from both local and federated storage, but line 86-87 still calls removeStoredCredentialById which only targets local/federated-storage, not the external CredentialInputUpdater. For external credentials, this removal would fail silently or target wrong store.

validated_findings.body: The recovery authenticator is considered configured, but rendering its input page throws NoSuchElementException (or fails to deserialize incomplete data), returning a server error instead of a login challenge.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Login form construction fails for otherwise valid CredentialInputUpdater/CredentialInputValidator implementations.
validated_findings.impact: The recovery authenticator is considered configured, but rendering its input page throws NoSuchElementException (or fails to deserialize incomplete data), returning a server error instead of a login challenge.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new external-storage path assumes that successful update/configuration implies availability of a complete CredentialModel through getFederatedCredentialsStream, although the SPI does not enforce that relationship and its retrieval method defaults to empty.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Do not unconditionally dereference the lookup. Define and enforce the full-model retrieval requirement for external recovery-code support, and gracefully treat a missing or incomplete model as unconfigured/setup-required or fall back to local storage during creation.
validated_findings.title: Configured external providers can produce an empty Optional and crash the login form
validated_findings.trigger: A user-storage provider supports updating and validating recovery codes and reports isConfiguredFor as true, but inherits CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()'s default empty stream or exposes only credential metadata.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 19 shows credentialModelOpt.get() is called unconditionally. RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential checks both stored and federated credentials, but if an external provider's getCredentials returns empty (the default per CredentialInputUpdater line 50-52), the Optional will be empty causing NoSuchElementException when isConfiguredFor returns true based on supportsCredentialType.

validated_findings.body: The external provider receives only the raw-code JSON and type, so it cannot recover credentialModel's generated timestamp or user label. Federated credential listings consequently expose missing or provider-invented metadata; the added test provider already substitutes the current time and loses the label.
validated_findings.evidence: UserCredentialModel recoveryCodesCredential = new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson);
validated_findings.failure_mode: Credential metadata differs depending on whether the credential was stored locally or externally.
validated_findings.impact: The external provider receives only the raw-code JSON and type, so it cannot recover credentialModel's generated timestamp or user label. Federated credential listings consequently expose missing or provider-invented metadata; the added test provider already substitutes the current time and loses the label.
validated_findings.root_cause: The helper accepts a complete RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel but reduces it to a plain UserCredentialModel containing only type and raw codes.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Define a recovery-code CredentialInput payload or notes that include the generated codes, generated-at value, and user label, and have user-storage implementations persist and return those fields.
validated_findings.title: The external credential input discards creation metadata and the user label
validated_findings.trigger: Recovery codes are saved to user storage with a non-null user label or with consumers expecting the generated-at timestamp from credentialModel to be preserved.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 123 shows UserCredentialModel constructed with only type and recoveryCodesJson. The credentialModel parameter contains createdDate and userLabel (from createFromValues), but these are not passed to the external provider. The test provider at line 239-240 uses recoveryCodes.getCreatedDate() and getUserLabel() which would be whatever the provider stored, not the original values.

validated_findings.body: Every attempt succeeds because validation never removes or marks the matched code as consumed. The new integration test's single successful login therefore gives false assurance for a credential that is required to be single-use.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A one-time recovery credential behaves as a permanently reusable credential in the external-storage test path.
validated_findings.impact: Every attempt succeeds because validation never removes or marks the matched code as consumed. The new integration test's single successful login therefore gives false assurance for a credential that is required to be single-use.
validated_findings.root_cause: The added validator performs a stateless membership check against the original raw-code list.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Persist consumption atomically when validation succeeds and add an integration assertion that immediately reusing the submitted code is rejected.
validated_findings.title: The test user-storage provider allows the same recovery code to be reused indefinitely
validated_findings.trigger: The same externally stored recovery code is submitted in two or more login attempts.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 340 shows 'generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))' - this performs a stateless check against all codes without removing the matched code. Recovery codes are single-use by design, but this test implementation allows unlimited reuse of any code.

validated_findings.body: The external provider accepts it, unlike RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider, which validates only getNextRecoveryAuthnCode(). The federated path therefore does not enforce the numbered prompt and tests do not exercise production-equivalent semantics.
validated_findings.failure_mode: External and local recovery-code authentication enforce different ordering rules.
validated_findings.impact: The external provider accepts it, unlike RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider, which validates only getNextRecoveryAuthnCode(). The federated path therefore does not enforce the numbered prompt and tests do not exercise production-equivalent semantics.
validated_findings.root_cause: Validation searches the entire stored list rather than selecting the next recovery-code entry.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Validate only the next expected code and preserve original code numbers as entries are consumed; add a test submitting a non-requested code and expecting rejection.
validated_findings.title: The test user-storage provider accepts a code other than the requested next code
validated_findings.trigger: The login page requests the first remaining numbered code, but the user submits any later code from the generated set.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 340 validates against any code in the list via anyMatch, while RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid (line 106-109 in context) only validates against getNextRecoveryAuthnCode(). The test provider accepts codes out of order, unlike production behavior.

validated_findings.body: createFromValues does not set an ID, and the code adds that new model without copying myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(). Credential listings therefore expose a null ID and ID-based lookup/removal cannot find the external credential.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Consumers cannot address the federated credential by ID.
validated_findings.impact: createFromValues does not set an ID, and the code adds that new model without copying myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(). Credential listings therefore expose a null ID and ID-based lookup/removal cannot find the external credential.
validated_findings.root_cause: The reconstruction copies code data and metadata but omits the identity assigned when the external credential was stored.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Set the reconstructed model's ID from myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() before adding it to the returned stream, and test listing and deleting the credential.
validated_findings.title: Federated recovery credential models are returned without their stored ID
validated_findings.trigger: Account management, CredentialDeleteHelper, or the authenticator attempts to identify or remove the recovery credential returned by this provider.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 242 adds model to credentialModels without setting an ID. RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues doesn't set ID (context line 58-84 shows no setId call). myUser.recoveryCodes has an ID but it's not copied to the reconstructed model, causing null ID in returned credentials.

validated_findings.body: disableCredentialType still only clears OTP credentials, so it logs recovery codes as unsupported and leaves them present. The credential also is not added to getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, leaving deletion behavior inconsistent with its removeable credential metadata.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Removal requests complete without removing the external recovery credential.
validated_findings.impact: disableCredentialType still only clears OTP credentials, so it logs recovery codes as unsupported and leaves them present. The credential also is not added to getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, leaving deletion behavior inconsistent with its removeable credential metadata.
validated_findings.root_cause: Recovery codes were added to supportsCredentialType without implementing the corresponding disable/removal side of the CredentialInputUpdater contract.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Handle RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE in disableCredentialType by clearing myUser.recoveryCodes and advertise the type from getDisableableCredentialTypesStream; add an external-credential deletion test.
validated_findings.title: The provider advertises recovery-code support but cannot disable that credential type
validated_findings.trigger: A user or administrator removes the externally stored recovery credential, causing SubjectCredentialManager.disableCredentialType to dispatch to this CredentialInputUpdater because supportsCredentialType now returns true.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 114 adds RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE to supportsCredentialType, but disableCredentialType (not shown in patch but referenced in context) only handles OTP types. getDisableableCredentialTypesStream at line 255-260 only adds OTP type. This inconsistency means recovery codes can't be properly disabled.

validated_findings.body: The fixture now imports modern recovery-code APIs and overrides modern credential-retrieval behavior that did not exist in the stated historical implementation. It can no longer substantiate the documented unchanged-provider compatibility claim.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The test and its documentation misrepresent what an actual unchanged 4.8.3 provider supports.
validated_findings.impact: The fixture now imports modern recovery-code APIs and overrides modern credential-retrieval behavior that did not exist in the stated historical implementation. It can no longer substantiate the documented unchanged-provider compatibility claim.
validated_findings.root_cause: New-feature behavior was implemented directly in a fixture documented as source-compatible historical code.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the 4.8.3 fixture unchanged and create a separate current user-storage test provider for recovery-code integration, or rename and redocument the fixture if preserving historical compatibility is no longer its purpose.
validated_findings.title: The historical backwards-compatibility fixture is no longer an unmodified 4.8.3 provider
validated_findings.trigger: The backwards-compatibility suite is used to determine whether a provider written for Keycloak 4.8.3 still works unchanged, as stated by this class's Javadoc.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 46 imports RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel which didn't exist in Keycloak 4.8.3. The class javadoc (line 58-60) states it's for backwards compatibility testing with 4.8.3, but adding modern recovery code support contradicts this purpose.
